blocks.markdown: **Method.** Start by **establishing coverage of the item**; then list the **legally required label information**, identify **additional rules for the product category**, and test for a **prohibited label or packaging act**. The statute includes special rules for products such as **food, drugs, cosmetics, hazardous substances and cigarettes**, so the general minimum label is not always the whole answer.
**Art. 77** addresses **minimum labeling requirements**; **Art. 79** permits **additional requirements** when authorized.
Arts. 80–94 include **product-specific rules** — always check the category rule on top of the general minimum.

A required label can serve **safety and informed-choice purposes**; it is not just packaging design. Check if information is **visible/legible, accurate, in the required language/form, and consistent with the nature of the regulated item**.
For price-tag questions, identify the **displayed price**, whether the item is **covered**, the rule on **sale at the tagged price**, and any **statutory exceptions**.

**Price tag vs. price ceiling:** a tag **discloses the seller's offered price**; a ceiling/freeze is a **statutory price control**. Do not confuse a price-tag violation with a price-control violation under RA 7581.
